question.knowledge_point: Determining the Position of a Particle Given Its Velocity and Initial Position
question.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=3$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
question.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(0))+C \\ 3 & =-\frac{1}{2}+C \\ C & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
x(t)=\frac{7}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).
$$
